text:
sarah: Customer reporting a rash of 502/504s hitting hosted inference during large embedding jobs. Happening for a few tenants, spike started ~08:22 UTC.
sarah: Quick repro they provided: curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{\"model\":\"embed-large\",\"input\":[\"long text... repeated ~2000 tokens\"]}'
sarah: Response: 502 with header \"x-edge-trace: trc_abc123\" and upstream \"502 upstream reset\" in body. Customer sees this intermittently at high concurrency.
ken: Can you paste the full response headers and the x-edge-trace? also want the tenant id and approximate qps/concurrency when it hit.
sarah: Trace: trc_abc123. Tenant: tenant-842. They were running ~14 concurrent embedding streams, each ~1.2k tokens, sustained for ~45s bursts. p95 latency reported ~2.1s before spike then errors. Headers: 
-----
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
x-edge-trace: trc_abc123
x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 
-----
body: {\"error\":\"upstream reset\"}
alex: I'm seeing an Envoy upstream reset pattern on the edge cluster around that trace. Logs show stream reset (RST_STREAM) with error code PROTOCOL_ERROR and a flurry of 0-length windows in h2 flow control. Snippet: 
```
[08:22:14] envoy envoy-cluster edge-proxy: stream 0x7f3c reset (PROTOCOL_ERROR) for upstream 10.2.4.11:8443
[08:22:14] envoy h2: window update mismatch, queued 0-window write
[08:22:15] envoy upstream conn 10.2.4.11:8443 -> reset
```
alex: Pattern looks like h2 connection window exhaustion / keepalive mismatch when many long-lived streams (embeddings) are open.
raj: This aligns with earlier h2-pool saturation cases. Tenant concurrency + long payloads leave small windows and triggers resets. Two likely levers: increase upstream initial window or increase connection pool size / keepalive settings; or shard requests to avoid single connection saturation.
sarah: Customer also attached an nginx frontdoor trace: 
```
proxy_time=08:22:14 status=502 backend=10.2.4.11:8443 \"RST_STREAM\" h2_streams=127 conn_pool=exhausted
```
ken: Can we check per-edge-instance H2 concurrent streams and keepalive counters for that time range? Also need to see if autoscaler injected new backends then or if upstream started returning 5xx.
deploy-bot: Deployment note: no deploys to edge cluster between 08:00-09:00 UTC. Rolling update last night.
alex: I pulled metrics: at 08:22 we hit ~95% of configured upstream conn pool on 3 of 6 edge hosts; active h2 streams spiked to ~220 on those instances (config allowed 128 max per connection). There are also many long-lived KV cache warmups for the model causing prolonged streams.
raj: Short-term mitigation we can try: 1) bump per-host upstream connection pool and per-connection max concurrent streams from defaults (128) to 256 for the affected edge pool, 2) enable aggressive keepalive pings to recycle stuck streams, 3) advise customer to chunk inputs or reduce concurrency while we experiment.
ken: Let's not flip pool globally. Can we apply a targeted config to the tenant's routing shard? If not, do a scoped override on the edge pool behind a feature flag. Also prepare rollback plan.
sarah: Customer agreed to throttle to 6 concurrent streams for now. They're reproducing with a small harness and will share a new trace id if it fails.
alex: I'll spin a canary with adjusted h2 window/streams on two hosts in us-west and route tenant-842 traffic there. If the rate of RST_STREAM drops we'll promote.
raj: Also capture tcpdump around reset to confirm it's flow-control/windowing (not TLS).
ken: Action items: alex -> canary config + metrics alert for RST_STREAM rate (20m). raj -> tcpdump & keepalive counters. sarah -> collect customer repro harness and new trace. I'll prepare a rollback to previous pool size.
sarah: customer sent new trace trc_def456 after throttling; looks successful so far (no 502s in next 6 minutes). We'll keep them at reduced concurrency while infra tests canary. :thumbsup:
alex: Canary applied, saw immediate drop in RST_STREAMs for tenant shard. We'll leave canary up for 30m and then promote if stable.
ken: Good. Postmortem candidate if this is repeatable—possible mitigations: smarter per-tenant connection sharding, per-request chunking guidance in docs, default lower per-connection streams for embedding-heavy models.
sarah: I'll follow up with customer once promote is done and add notes to the ticket.
raj: Filing a follow-up runbook entry for h2-windowing/embedding workloads.
sarah: Thanks all.
